In the rest frame of the pion the total energy is just the pion mass‑energy  

\[
E_{\pi}=m_{\pi}c^{2}=139.6\ {\rm MeV}.
\]

Let the muon have kinetic energy \(K_{\mu}\) and the (practically massless) neutrino have kinetic energy \(K_{\nu}=E_{\nu}=pc\).  
Momentum conservation requires the muon and neutrino to have equal and opposite momenta \(p\).  

\[
E_{\pi}=E_{\mu}+E_{\nu}= \sqrt{p^{2}c^{2}+m_{\mu}^{2}c^{4}} + pc .
\]

Setting \(c=1\) (MeV units) and solving for \(p\):

\[
\sqrt{p^{2}+m_{\mu}^{2}} = m_{\pi}-p
\]

\[
p^{2}+m_{\mu}^{2}=m_{\pi}^{2}-2m_{\pi}p+p^{2}
\]

\[
2m_{\pi}p=m_{\pi}^{2}-m_{\mu}^{2}
\]

\[
p=\frac{m_{\pi}^{2}-m_{\mu}^{2}}{2m_{\pi}} .
\]

Insert the numbers (with \(c=1\)):

\[
p=\frac{(139.6)^{2}-(105.7)^{2}}{2\times139.6}
   =\frac{19488.16-11172.49}{279.2}
   \approx 29.8\ {\rm MeV}/c .
\]

Hence the neutrino kinetic energy  

\[
K_{\nu}=E_{\nu}=pc\approx 29.8\ {\rm MeV}.
\]

The muon’s total energy is  

\[
E_{\mu}=m_{\pi}c^{2}-pc\approx 139.6-29.8=109.8\ {\rm MeV},
\]

so its kinetic energy  

\[
K_{\mu}=E_{\mu}-m_{\mu}c^{2}=109.8-105.7\approx 4.1\ {\rm MeV}.
\]

Rounded to two decimal places:

- Muon kinetic energy ≈ 4.12 MeV  
- Neutrino kinetic energy ≈ 29.8 MeV  

These values correspond to choice **(A)**.

**Answer: A**
